reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection treats every corpus row with demand_score >= 3 as demand-bearing, but the supplied package only shows bare need strings, scores, and source weights. It does not show observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes supporting those demand claims, so the selection rests on asserted scores/generic need text rather than validated market-demand evidence.

evidence_normalization preserves the selected records, constrains record identifiers to the allowed n06-r01 through n06-r08 set, normalizes numeric fields, and applies the explicit bounded eight-row window. The visible input and output hashes remain consistent through this boundary, so no behaviorally significant normalization fault is localized here.

provenance_assembly deterministically ranks the normalized needs by descending demand_score with record_id tie-breaks and assembles the evidence_sources handoff records. Its output matches the assigned job evidence_sources ordering, and the package records exact hash handoffs for both needs and evidence_sources, so no local fault is indicated in this boundary.
